scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC3 and PC4 in Campus 2 VLAN 6 report their gateway (10.6.0.254)
no longer responds. Other Campus 2 PCs (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5 on
VLAN 5) are fine. Identify the misconfiguration.

injection.action: change br_v6 SVI IP from .254 to .200
injection.command:
ip addr del 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6
  ip addr add 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v6 SVI IP address
Mechanism: PCs have their default route hard-coded to
  10.6.0.254 (the standard Cisco SVI VRRP-style address).
  sshswitch's br_v6 was reconfigured to 10.6.0.200, so
  ARP for 10.6.0.254 gets no reply — packets can't egress
  the subnet. The new address .200 IS reachable, but no host
  knows to use it.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v6 SVI IP set to 10.6.0.200 instead of 10.6.0.254
Fix: re-set the IP — `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 &&
  ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`
scenario.fix_spec:
re-set the IP — `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 &&
  ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: br_v6 SVI IP / VLAN 6 gateway IP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a misconfigured IP address on the VLAN 6 SVI (switched virtual interface) of `sshswitch`. `sshswitch` acts as the Layer 3 gateway for both VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 in the Campus 2 segment. Its VLAN 5 SVI (`br_v5`) is correctly assigned `10.5.0.254/24`, which is why PC1, PC2, and dc_pc5 on VLAN 5 work normally. However, its VLAN 6 SVI (`br_v6`) was configured with `10.6.0.200/24` instead of the expected `10.6.0.254/24`.

PC3 (`10.6.0.3`) and PC4 (`10.6.0.4`) both have their default gateway set to `10.6.0.254`, which is the intended gateway address. Because no device in the lab holds that IP, ARP resolution for `10.6.0.254` yields no reply and every off-subnet packet sent by PC3/PC4 is dropped immediately with "Destination Host Unreachable". Pinging `10.6.0.200` (the actual SVI address) from PC3 succeeds with full connectivity, confirming that the data path through the switch fabric and VLAN 6 trunk is intact — only the gateway IP itself is wrong.

Root cause: The VLAN 6 SVI on `sshswitch` was assigned `10.6.0.200/24` in the startup configuration instead of the correct `10.6.0.254/24`.

Corrective fix: Change the `br_v6` interface address on `sshswitch` from `10.6.0.200/24` to `10.6.0.254/24` (e.g., `ip addr del 10.6.0.200/24 dev br_v6 && ip addr add 10.6.0.254/24 dev br_v6`), and update the persistent startup script accordingly so the fix survives a restart.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names `sshswitch` as the device with the misconfigured br_v6 SVI.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the br_v6 SVI on VLAN 6 as misconfigured (set to 10.6.0.200 instead of the expected gateway 10.6.0.254).
Proposes removing the wrong IP and assigning 10.6.0.254/24 to br_v6 (and persisting it), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's log contains the key observations (br_v6 = 10.6.0.200, successful ping to .200, failed pings to .254, VLAN5 .254 reachable) that directly support the diagnosis. Minor gaps: explicit ip route outputs / startup-file evidence are not shown, but the inference that the wrong SVI IP causes ARP failure and loss of gateway is well supported.
